note: Schematic/illustrative geometry for study. Seasons follow the month slider. Sources: CLIMATE_PHENOMENA_TODO.md

items.name: Southwest monsoon onset over Kerala
items.label: SW monsoon onset — Kerala (normal 1 Jun)
items.info: IMD declares onset when 60% of 14 designated Kerala stations report ≥2.5 mm rain for 2 consecutive days, westerlies hold to 600 hPa and INSAT OLR <200 W m⁻². Normal date 1 June; opens India's principal rainy season.

items.name: Northern Limit of Monsoon (progressive advance)
items.label: NLM — normal mid-Jul cover
items.info: Monsoon advances in surges; the Northern Limit of Monsoon is the northernmost position reached. The country is normally fully covered around 8 July (2020 revised normals; legacy normal 15 July).

items.name: Withdrawal of SW monsoon (retreating monsoon)
items.label: Withdrawal Oct–Dec (NW first, peninsula last)
items.info: No withdrawal before 1 Sept; declared on 5-day rainfall cessation + 850-hPa anticyclone. NW India withdraws first (delayed >2 weeks vs the legacy 1 Sept normal); country-wide withdrawal only after 1 Oct, completed ~15 Oct.

items.name: Active & break monsoon spells (intraseasonal variability)
items.label: Active/break core — central India
items.info: Active/vigorous spells: rainfall 1.5–4× / >4× normal; break monsoon: trough shifts to the Himalayan foothills → foothill floods + dry central India. Driven by the 40-day mode, 14–15-day quasi-biweekly oscillation and the MJO.

items.name: Monsoon trough
items.label: Monsoon trough — Ganganagar→Head Bay
items.info: Semi-permanent elongated low from the heat low (NW Rajasthan–Pakistan) to the Head Bay; normal axis Ganganagar–Allahabad–Kolkata–Head Bay, oscillating ~5° daily. South of axis = active monsoon; north/foothills = break.

items.name: Monsoon lows & depressions
items.label: NW Bay genesis zone
items.info: Principal rain-bearing systems; lows intensify into depressions (17–33 kt), ~2 per monsoon month. Genesis north of 18°N in the NW Bay (Jul–Aug), shifting to the central Bay in Sept; heaviest rain in the SW quadrant.

items.name: Northeast (winter) monsoon
items.label: NE monsoon — Oct–Dec
items.info: Oct–Dec reversal to northeasterlies — main rainy season of the south peninsula, ~60% of coastal Tamil Nadu annual rain. 2025 commencement announced 16 Oct over TN–Puducherry, coastal AP, Rayalaseema, S interior Karnataka, Kerala.

items.name: Subtropical westerly jet (winter)
items.label: Westerly jet ~27N, ~12 km (winter)
items.info: Steady westerly jet at ~27°N, ~200 hPa (~12 km). Shifts north of the Himalayas at monsoon onset (permitting the SW monsoon); dips south in winter and break phases with western disturbances.

items.name: Tropical easterly jet (summer)
items.label: Easterly jet ~13N, ~15 km (Jul)
items.info: Upper-level easterly jet at ~150 hPa in July, centred near Chennai's latitude, Vietnam → West Africa (Tibetan High outflow). Strong/south of normal in active spells; weak/shifted north (~20°N) in breaks.

items.name: ITCZ shift over India
items.label: ITCZ at Jul normal (~13N)
items.info: The equatorial trough/ITCZ migrates from ~5°S (January) to 12–15°N (July); its northward march and merging with the heat trough governs onset and advance. Drawn at the July normal; the slider gates its season.

items.name: Tibetan Plateau heating (Tibetan High)
items.label: Tibetan High
items.info: Intense heating of the elevated plateau builds a warm upper anticyclone (max intensity 200 hPa); outflow feeds the easterly jet and its position steers monsoon lows and rainfall.

items.name: Heat low over NW India & seasonal migration
items.label: Heat low migration Mar→Jun
items.info: Land–ocean thermal contrast drives the seasonal wind reversal; the shallow heat low (to 850 hPa) over NW Rajasthan–Pakistan acts as a suction device along the trough. Migrates: Mar peninsula → Apr Vidarbha/MP → May Punjab → Jun–Sep NW Rajasthan.

items.name: Western Ghats orography, off-shore trough & rain shadow
items.label: Western Ghats orographic rain + rain shadow
items.info: Monsoon winds striking the Ghats form an off-shore vortex; the off-shore trough (to ~0.9 km) gives heavy west-coast rain (Mahabaleshwar extreme; Pune in rain shadow).

items.name: Mawsynram & Cherrapunji (Khasi Hills) extreme rainfall
items.label: Mawsynram / Cherrapunji
items.info: The Khasi Hills of Meghalaya funnel the monsoon; Cherrapunji and Mawsynram record world-class rainfall totals, studied in IMD's MAUSAM journal.

items.name: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO)
items.label: ENSO (Pacific, off-map edge)
items.info: Coupled Pacific ocean–atmosphere mode, events recur every 2–7 yrs, peak Nov–Feb. El Niño generally suppresses the ISM (droughts 1982/87/2002/09/15); La Niña strengthens it. Inverse but not deterministic (~42% of El Niño years below normal, IMD Pune).

link.note: El Niño → weak SW monsoon; La Niña → strong (not deterministic)

items.name: ENSO Modoki (central-Pacific El Niño)
items.label: ENSO Modoki
items.info: Central-Pacific warm tripole (ENSO Modoki Index, Ashok et al. 2007) with distinct teleconnections; Modoki–IOD combinations make NIO cyclogenesis complex (more frequent cyclones in some combinations).

items.name: Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD; 'Indian Niño')
items.label: IOD poles — DMI = west−east SST anomaly
items.info: SST seesaw: western pole 50–70°E/10°S–10°N, eastern pole 90–110°E/10°S–0°; DMI = west − east anomaly (event when |DMI|≥0.4 °C sustained). Positive IOD favours above-normal ISMR and can offset El Niño (1997, 2019, DMI to +1.78).

link.note: +IOD → above-normal monsoon (can offset El Niño); −IOD → below

items.name: Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO)
items.label: MJO — eastward 30–60-day pulse
items.info: Eastward-moving planetary pulse (8 phases, ~7–8 days each). Drives active/break spells beyond ~1 week; monsoon genesis favoured in phases 4–5, post-monsoon phases 3–4.

items.name: Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO)
items.label: PDO (Pacific)
items.info: Slow Pacific SST pattern; IMD's Monsoon FAQ lists PDO among the year-to-year ISM factors (with NAO). IPO: no direct IMD material found (marginal).

link.note: PDO is one of the year-to-year ISM factors (with NAO)

items.name: Indian Ocean Basin Mode (IOBM) / Indian Ocean warming
items.label: IOBM — basin-wide warm mode
items.info: Dominant interannual tropical-Indian-Ocean SST mode; warm IOB peaks in spring and its extra moisture is transported to South Asia. Post-1951 ~1 °C warming weakens the land–sea thermal gradient (IITM), drying central-east India.

items.name: North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) & AMO
items.label: NAO / AMO (Atlantic, off-map edge)
items.info: NAO is listed by IMD among ISM-influencing factors (no strong deterministic fetched link). Positive AMO decades coincide with wetter ISM (e.g. 1926–65); paleo-records show coherent response over central India.

link.note: +AMO decades → wetter ISM; NAO listed as an ISM factor

items.name: Tropical cyclones over the North Indian Ocean
items.label: NIO cyclone seasons (Nov & May peaks)
items.info: RSMC New Delhi watches the basin round-the-clock: two peaks (Apr–May, Oct–Dec; November maximum). ~5 cyclones/yr ≈ 5–6% of the global average; 4:1 Bay:Arabian ratio; 2024 saw 13 vs 11.2 normal.

items.name: IMD intensity classification scale
items.label: IMD scale: D→DD→CS→SCS→VSCS→ESCS→SuCS
items.info: Depression (31–49 km/h) → Deep Depression → Cyclonic Storm → Severe (89–117) → Very Severe (118–166) → Extremely Severe (167–221) → Super Cyclonic Storm (≥222 km/h). WMO-adopted standard driving warning levels.

items.name: Storm surge / storm tide
items.label: Storm-surge coasts (illustrative strips)
items.info: Wind-driven sea-level rise at landfall on top of the astronomical tide — 'by far the greatest killers in a cyclone'. Most exposed: low-lying deltas of Odisha, West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat. Strips are illustrative.

items.name: Western Disturbance
items.label: Western disturbance track
items.info: Cyclonic circulation/trough in the mid-latitude westerlies from the Mediterranean/Caspian/Black Sea region across Iraq–Iran–Afghanistan–Pakistan into NW India; principal winter precipitation source (~6–7/month Dec–Feb), beneficial for rabi crops.

items.name: Nor'wester / Kalbaisakhi
items.label: Nor'wester / Kalbaisakhi (max May)
items.info: Severe pre-monsoon convective thunderstorms and squalls of eastern/NE India (IMD field studies since 1931–41; STORM programme 2007–2010). Cells initiate over Jharkhand/Odisha/Bangladesh and organize into mesoscale complexes. 'Bardoli Chheerha' local name not found on fetched IMD pages.

items.name: Dust storms / Andhi
items.label: Andhi / dust storms — Rajasthan
items.info: Convective sand/dust storms of NW India (Apr–Jun); with little moisture, downdrafts from cumulonimbus raise dust. Visibility below 1 km; triggered by intense surface heating plus WDs/cyclonic circulations.

items.name: Thunderstorms, hailstorms & squall lines
items.label: Thunderstorm / hail zones
items.info: Pre-monsoon (Mar–May) is India's peak convective season; violent thunderstorms, squalls, heavy precipitation and hail common over NE India. Squall lines are mesoscale lines of storms; parent phenomena of Andhi and Nor'wester.

items.name: Tornadoes
items.label: Tornado cases (44 in IMD record)
items.info: Rare over India: IMD records yielded 44 tornado cases (+113 strong-wind reports from 1951); preferred zones are mesoscale lows along lines of discontinuity at the tail of violent thunderstorms. Dot cluster is illustrative.

items.name: Heat wave / severe heat wave (warm night)
items.label: Heat-wave zones (peak May)
items.info: Station max ≥40 °C plains / ≥37 coast / ≥30 hills; departure 4.5–6.4 °C = heat wave, >6.4 °C severe. Mar–Jun (peak May); NW & central 'heat belt' plus AP/Odisha coast. May 2015 SE-India event: >2,500 deaths.

items.name: Loo
items.label: Loo — Punjab/Haryana/E.Rajasthan/UP
items.info: Hot, dry, oppressive pre-monsoon wind — a 'marked feature of summers in northern India' (IMD); blows from afternoon into midnight; evening dust storms common in May.

items.name: Cold wave / severe cold wave (cold day)
items.label: Cold-wave zone (worst Dec–Jan)
items.info: Station min ≤10 °C plains / ≤0 hills; departure −4.5 to −6.4 °C = cold wave, ≤−6.4 severe. Nov–Mar, worst Dec–Jan in NW/central India; Jan 2003 ~900 deaths; frequency decreasing as winter minimums warm.

items.name: Winter fog
items.label: Winter fog — Indo-Gangetic plains
items.info: Large-scale episodic IGP fog spells lasting weeks (Dec–Jan peak); radiation fog after western disturbances. Densest spells drop visibility below 50 m; 12 airports get IMD fog warnings; ~120–159 road deaths in the worst 2016–18 seasons. The most fog-vulnerable region globally per IMD.

items.name: Frost / ground frost
items.label: Frost — NW plains & foothills
items.info: Frost 'prevails when temperature falls below 0 °C in an area where it is abnormal'; NDMA/IMD criterion: winds <16 km/h and air temp <0 °C on sub-zero winter nights. Rabi crop losses; ≥33% loss qualifies for national relief.

items.name: Mango showers
items.label: Mango / blossom showers
items.info: End-of-summer pre-monsoon showers of Kerala and coastal Karnataka (not an IMD criteria term); hasten mango ripening and make coffee flower ('blossom'/'cherry-blossom' showers). Beneficial before the monsoon.

items.name: October heat
items.label: October heat — post-monsoon peninsula
items.info: Retreating SW monsoon brings clear skies and rising temperatures over still-moist land; combined heat and humidity make weather 'oppressive' — the 'October heat'; the mercury then falls rapidly over north India.

items.name: Urban heat island (UHI) effect
items.label: Urban heat islands — major metros
items.info: Cities run hotter than surroundings; NDMA's 2019 heat guidelines require UHI assessment in Heat Action Plans (23 states, 195 districts, 64 cities). Worst on summer nights; Delhi SAPCC 2.0: summer max projected +1.5 °C (SSP2-4.5) to +2.1 °C (SSP5-8.5) by the 2050s.

items.name: Atmospheric brown cloud (ABC)
items.label: Atmospheric brown cloud — IGP + N Indian Ocean
items.info: Haze of sulphates, nitrates, organics, black carbon, dust and fly ash; dominant over India in winter, low in the summer monsoon (INDOEX 1996–99). Solar dimming; anthropogenic aerosols linked to the post-1950s ISM rainfall decline, while IGP absorbing aerosols can invigorate pre-monsoon rain.

items.name: Global warming signals for India
items.label: India warming trend
items.info: Surface air temperature over India rose ~0.7 °C (1901–2018); tropical Indian Ocean SST +~1 °C (1951–2015). Rising heavy-rain/drought extremes, higher TC intensity; IMD Climate Hazard & Vulnerability Atlas + 29 state rainfall-variability reports.

items.name: Himalayan cryosphere & GLOF risk
items.label: Glacier retreat / GLOF lakes
items.info: HKH glaciers retreating 14.9±15.1 m/yr (Ganga 15.5±14.4, Brahmaputra 20.2±19.7); Chandra basin lost ~6% area in 20 yrs. New/enlarging glacial lakes raise GLOF risk; NGRMP phase-I early warning (HP, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal, J&K, Ladakh).

items.name: Sea-level rise (MoES/INCOIS)
items.label: Sea-level rise — tide-gauge trends (mm/yr)
items.info: North Indian Ocean ~3.3 mm/yr (1993–2015); 1993–2020 altimeter trends 4.1–4.6 mm/yr at Mumbai, Mormugao, Kochi, Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Paradip. Erosion, saline intrusion; INCOIS hazard line guides adaptation.
